## Loading in the data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(glmnet)

train <- read_csv("data-train.csv")

# Calculate the four target statistics
train <- train %>%
  mutate(
    m1 = R_moment_1,
    m2 = R_moment_2,
    m3 = R_moment_3,
    m4 = R_moment_4,

    C_moment_2 = m2 - m1^2,
    C_moment_3 = m3 - 3*m1*m2 + 2*m1^3,
    C_moment_4 = m4 - 4*m1*m3 + 6*m1^2*m2 - 3*m1^4,

    sd_R = sqrt(C_moment_2),
    skewness = C_moment_3 / sd_R^3,
    kurtosis = C_moment_4 / sd_R^4,
    ex_kurt = kurtosis - 3,
  )

# Only use the three input parameters as predictors
X <- train %>%
  select(Re, Fr, St)

# The four required outcomes
Y <- train %>%
  select(R_moment_1, sd_R, skewness, kurtosis)

# Check for Y
summary(Y)
```
```{r}
train |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = St, y = skewness, color = as.factor(Re), shape = as.factor(Fr))) +
  geom_point()
```

everything is very right skewed - which is why we end up trying Box Cox transformation

```{r}

train %>%
```

## Model Fitting

```{r}
train <- train %>%
  mutate(log_St = log(St))

pairwise <- paste0(
  "Re * Fr_invlogit + ",
  "Re * log_St + ",
  "Fr_invlogit * log_St"
)

models <- list(
  M1_linear = skewness ~ Re + Fr_invlogit + log_St,

  M2_pairwise = as.formula(
    paste("skewness ~", pairwise)
  ),

  M3_quadratic_only =
    skewness ~ Re + Fr_invlogit + log_St +
    I(Re^2) + I(Fr_invlogit^2) + I(log_St^2),

  M4_pairwise_S2 = as.formula(
    paste("skewness ~", pairwise, "+ I(log_St^2)")
  ),

  M5_pairwise_R2_S2 = as.formula(
    paste("skewness ~", pairwise,
          "+ I(Re^2) + I(log_St^2)")
  ),

  M6_pairwise_F2_S2 = as.formula(
    paste("skewness ~", pairwise,
          "+ I(Fr_invlogit^2) + I(log_St^2)")
  ),

  M7_full_quadratic = as.formula(
    paste("skewness ~", pairwise,
          "+ I(Re^2) + I(Fr_invlogit^2) + I(log_St^2)")
  ),

  M8_three_way =
    skewness ~ Re * Fr_invlogit * log_St,

  M9_three_way_selected_squares =
    skewness ~ Re * Fr_invlogit * log_St +
    I(Re^2) + I(log_St^2)
)
```


```{r}
# Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation
ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "LOOCV"
)

# Fit and compare all models
results <- lapply(names(models), function(nm) {
  fit <- caret::train(
    models[[nm]],
    data = train,
    method = "lm",
    trControl = ctrl,
    metric = "RMSE"
  )

  tibble(
    model = nm,
    RMSE = fit$results$RMSE[1],
    MAE = fit$results$MAE[1]
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  arrange(RMSE)

print(results)
```
doing RMSE/MAE how erin did:
```{r}
loo_rmse <- function(m) sqrt(mean((resid(m) / (1 - hatvalues(m)))^2))
# Compare LOOCV RMSE across all models
results <- lapply(names(models), function(nm) {
  m <- lm(models[[nm]], data = train)

  tibble(
    model = nm,
    RMSE = loo_rmse(m)
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  arrange(RMSE)

print(results)
```
